data.name: Jerald
data.long_meaning: The name Jerald originated from the Germanic word 'ger-wulf', meaning 'spear-wolf'. It was popularized by the Normans during the Middle Ages and adopted into various European languages. In Christian tradition, Jerald represents the strength and protection of a ruler, making it a fitting name for a son.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name imbued with the spirit of courage and leadership.
data.numerology_meaning: People with the name Jerald are natural leaders and innovators, with a strong will and the ability to inspire others.

in_latin.name: Jeraldus
in_latin.long_meaning: Jeraldus nomen derivatum est ab Hebraico 'Jerald'. Nomen significat fortitudo et fortis. Historia docet quod Jeraldus fuit unus ex primis Apostolis. Apostolus Paulus scripsit quod Jeraldus fuit unus ex personalibus suis fratribus.

It is often associated with qualities such as leadership, determination, and a strong sense of faith. In the context of biblical names, Jerald is also seen as a symbol of spiritual strength and perseverance.

data.spiritual_significance: Jerald is a reminder of the protective and defensive nature of God, as represented by a spear or a shield in battle. The name inspires one to be a champion of righteousness and a defender of faith. It also serves as a reminder to remain strong in the face of adversity, drawing inspiration from the biblical figure of Jerrald or Jael, the heroine who defeated Sisera with a tent peg.
